profile.name: Ali Hariz Bin Anuari
profile.headline: Software engineer · Malaysia
profile.intro: I like systems that people already depend on. A decade-old finance tool nobody wanted to touch, a queue of thousands of unread complaints, a road network too big to inspect by hand — I take those apart and rebuild them so they run in a browser, explain themselves, and keep working after I've gone. Most of what's here runs on a small computer in my house.

items.title: HARDA — Hazard Assessment Road Detection
items.subtitle: Final Year Project
items.shortDescription: Road hazards photographed by the public, classified by a fine-tuned YOLOv8 model, geotagged from image EXIF and plotted on a live map — with an admin workflow for verification, crew assignment and resolution tracking.
items.description: A three-tier system that automates road hazard reporting in Malaysia. A member of the public photographs a hazard from the web app or the mobile app; the backend runs YOLOv8 inference, extracts GPS from the image EXIF data (falling back to device location), and files the report. Local authority admins verify submissions, assign them to regional field crews, and track them through to resolution, with an after-photo closing the loop. Built as a Flask REST API over PostgreSQL, a React web client, and a React Native app that serves both public reporters and field crew from the same codebase.
items.problem: Road hazards are under-reported and manual inspection does not scale across a national road network. Existing reporting tools also lose their history once a hazard is settled, so authorities cannot see what was fixed, when, or by whom — a gap identified with an ex-Roadcare site supervisor during requirements gathering.
items.solution: YOLOv8 fine-tuned on a road-damage dataset classifies hazards above a 0.70 confidence threshold, with all detections above the threshold returned so one photograph can carry several hazards. EXIF GPS geotags each report, and a resolved-hazard archive with before and after photographs preserves the history that comparable systems discard.
items.myRole: Sole developer across the whole system: requirements and stakeholder interviews, database design (9 tables), the Flask API, the YOLO inference service, the React dashboard, the cross-platform mobile app, and the deployment. Now self-hosted on my own hardware behind a Cloudflare Tunnel rather than a cloud provider.
items.outcome: Delivered and running in production on self-hosted infrastructure at harda.aliharizanuari.org. Twelve use cases across three clients — web, Android and iOS — served by one API. Rate limiting and English/Malay localisation, both non-functional requirements the design document called for, were implemented and verified.
achievements: Fine-tuned YOLOv8 on road-damage data with multi-hazard detection above a 0.70 confidence threshold
Designed a 9-table schema supporting admin verification, regional crew assignment and a resolved-hazard audit archive
Shipped 3 clients — React web, Android and iOS — against a single Flask REST API
Implemented EXIF GPS extraction with device-location fallback for photographs missing geotags
Bilingual interface in English and Malay across both web and mobile
Self-hosted end to end: Docker Compose, Caddy and a Cloudflare Tunnel, with no cloud provider

items.title: Breathe Easy: Respiratory System Explorer
items.subtitle: Interactive Educational Web Application
items.shortDescription: Interactive educational website for learning about the human respiratory system with animations, quizzes, and 3D models
items.description: Developed an interactive educational web application designed to teach biology students about the human respiratory system. The website features interactive anatomy diagrams, breathing animations and simulations, knowledge quizzes, embedded 3D models, and comprehensive disease information—all built with modern vanilla JavaScript using ES6 modules.
items.problem: Biology students often struggle to visualize and understand the complex mechanics of the respiratory system through static textbook diagrams. There was a need for an engaging, interactive learning tool that could make respiratory anatomy and physiology more accessible.
items.solution: Built a comprehensive educational platform with multiple interactive features: clickable anatomy diagrams that display detailed information about each respiratory organ, animated breathing simulations showing the inhalation/exhalation process, embedded 3D Sketchfab models for spatial understanding, and gamified quizzes to test knowledge retention.
items.myRole: Full-stack developer responsible for the entire application architecture. Designed the modular JavaScript structure with separate classes for navigation, anatomy diagrams, breathing animations, and quiz functionality. Implemented responsive CSS with custom properties and created smooth animations for enhanced user engagement.
items.outcome: Created a fully functional educational resource that provides an immersive learning experience. The modular codebase makes it easy to extend with additional content, and the responsive design ensures accessibility across all devices.
achievements: Built modular JavaScript architecture with 6+ reusable class modules (Navigation, AnatomyDiagram, BreathingAnimation, BreathingSimulation, Quiz, Utils)
Implemented interactive image map with clickable anatomy regions displaying detailed organ information
Created dynamic breathing simulation with real-time oxygen level tracking and animated visuals
Developed comprehensive quiz system with randomized questions, scoring, and answer review functionality
Integrated 3D Sketchfab models for immersive anatomical exploration
Designed responsive layout with CSS custom properties and smooth scroll navigation
responsibilities: Modular JavaScript architecture design using ES6 classes and modules
Interactive UI/UX implementation with animations and transitions

sections.title: The homelab
sections.body: An HP EliteDesk 800 G2 Mini in Negeri Sembilan running everything on this domain: Docker Compose behind Caddy, exposed through a Cloudflare Tunnel with no ports open on the router, reached privately over Tailscale. It hosts this site, HARDA, Nextcloud, uptime monitoring and a Minecraft server, and backs itself up nightly.
